descriptionChirho: Deep, intense anger or indignation, used both of divine wrath (God's righteous fury against sin) and of human anger; the core semantic concept is the same across all 36 occurrences with variation being purely grammatical (nominative, accusative, genitive, dative). Multilingual evidence: spa 'ira' in both clusters, hin 'क्रोध' (krodh, fierce anger) throughout, arb 'الغَضَبِ/غَضَبُ/غَضَبِي' all from root غ-ض-ب (ghadab, wrath), kor '진노' (jinno, wrath) in both, swa 'ghadhabu' (divine fury) and 'hasira' (anger) reflect register difference rather than distinct senses. Covers Romans 1:18, Ephesians 2:3, Revelation 6:16-17 and similar passages.
